unit.title: The Pluperfect Subjunctive
unit.subtitle: Regrets and hypotheticals about the completed past

grammar.title: The subjunctive for the past-before-the-past
grammar.intro: The pluperfect subjunctive (pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo) expresses a completed, hypothetical past inside a subjunctive context. It's a compound tense: take the imperfect subjunctive of haber (hubiera) and add a past participle. Think of it as the subjunctive version of 'I had done' — perfect for regrets and things that never happened.

sections.heading: hubiera + past participle
sections.body: Conjugate haber in the imperfect subjunctive, then add the participle (which never changes). The nosotros form takes a written accent. An -iese variant also exists (hubiese hablado) with the exact same meaning:

ex.en: I wish I had studied more.
I didn't think we had gone.

sections.heading: Watch the irregular participles
sections.body: The participle carries the meaning, so the irregular ones matter. Memorise these — they show up constantly:

ex.en: I wish I had done it earlier.
I didn't think they had come back.

sections.heading: When you need it
sections.body: Use it after a past-tense trigger that demands the subjunctive, but where the action is already completed — one step further back than the imperfect subjunctive. Classic homes: Ojalá for regrets, and emotion/doubt verbs in the past:

ex.en: I was glad you had come.

ex.es: Habría sido mejor que hubiera sido honesto.
ex.en: It would have been better if he had been honest.

takeaways: Forms: hubiera, hubieras, hubiera, hubiéramos, hubierais, hubieran.
It marks a completed, hypothetical past: Ojalá hubiera estudiado más.
Irregular participles matter: hecho, visto, dicho, escrito, vuelto, puesto.

mistakes.w: Ojalá viniera a la fiesta de ayer.
mistakes.r: Ojalá hubiera venido a la fiesta de ayer.
mistakes.why: For a regret about a completed past event, use the pluperfect subjunctive, not the imperfect subjunctive.
hacer has an irregular participle: hecho, not 'hacido'.

mistakes.w: Me alegré de que hubieras venir.
mistakes.r: Me alegré de que hubieras venido.
mistakes.why: After hubieras you need a past participle (venido), not an infinitive.

exercises.prompt_en: I wish I had studied more.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! Un lamento del pasado → hubiera estudiado.
exercises.no: A completed-past regret needs the pluperfect subjunctive: “hubiera estudiado”.

exercises.prompt_en: I didn't think they had come back.
exercises.no: Doubt in the past + a completed action: “hubieran vuelto” (volver → vuelto).

exercises.prompt: Build: “I was glad you had come.”
exercises.no: “Me alegré de que hubieras venido” — hubieras plus the participle venido.

exercises.prompt_en: I wish I had done it earlier.
exercises.hint: hubiera + the irregular participle of hacer.
exercises.no: It's “hubiera hecho” — hacer has the irregular participle hecho.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb to its past participle.

exercises.translation: I wish I had studied more.
exercises.no: It was: “Ojalá hubiera estudiado más.” (I wish I had studied more.)

exercises.scenario: A friend missed a great party 🎉

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.es: La fiesta de anoche fue increíble. ¡Qué pena que no vinieras!
lines.en: Last night's party was amazing. What a shame you didn't come!

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Un lamento del pasado → hubiera ido.
exercises.no: A regret about a completed past uses the pluperfect subjunctive: “ojalá hubiera ido”.

exercises.en: I wish I had come earlier.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “Ojalá hubiera venido antes.”
